extraction.Name: Louis Deon
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent to his allotment, but he was told by the employees of the Agency that his patent was here, and that he might just as well take it, because he would have to pay taxes whether he got it or not, and he came after the patent and siged for it
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold the place in 1922, to a man by the name of Gates, receiving Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000.00) in cash for same, it being free from all encumbrance
extraction.Buyer: a man by the name of Gates, for Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000.00) in cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: never had this place mortgaged; and kept taxes paid at all times
extraction.Occupation/Income: works as a carpenter for the United States Government. This is his only revenue.
extraction.NOTES: Mentally competent; enjoying good health; financial circumstances are rather poor; has a wife and seven children — three children grown and self-supporting, and four depending upon him for support — entire family have good health; has never received any aid from the County or Government; document sworn November 10, 1928, County of Shannon, State of South Dakota
